correctness.rationale: The full proof identifies a saturated rank-1 scroll line from C~2H+(g−2)f, then the cubic-scroll normal quotient via 0→O_S(2f)→O_S(H+f)^3→N_S→0. Restriction gives the complete evaluation dual for D=LA^−1 with π_*D=O⊕O(1), and a snake-lemma sequence identifies its degree-g subline with quotient A of degree two. The lifted rank-(1,2,3) normal flag has line quotients degrees (4g+4,2g+6,g+8), strictly decreasing for every g≥3; it is therefore the HN filtration. Determinant and degree agree with adjunction; checker confirms finite arithmetic but is not used as infinite proof. Critical normal resolutions are justified in primary text and independently reconstructed.

originality.rationale: The identified three-step HN graded line bundles and their strictly descending degrees for every g≥3 lie beyond the binary stability assertion and single scroll destabilizer established in Liu 2026. Liu’s refined large-rank scroll-core lemma requires r≥g+2, whereas the claimed class has r=3. Coskun–Jovinelly–Larson 2026 explicitly treat the comparable genus-two case, which is excluded; their general Brill–Noether stability theorem does not cover HN on the hyperelliptic locus. Targeted mathematical-record and primary full-text searches found no dominating HN theorem for g≥3. Existence of an unindexed or implicit prior derivation remains a specific residual risk.

value.rationale: The natural missing invariant is the entire HN filtration, not the already-known boolean instability for special hyperelliptic embeddings. Its three exact slopes and canonical intermediate rank-two step quantify the instability across all genera g≥3 in P4 and distinguish hyperelliptic special-locus bundles from the generic Brill–Noether stability landscape. This is a natural complete structural classification, not an arbitrary parameter slice or renaming of the existing first destabilizing line. No claim is made about extension splitting or downstream applications.
